A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same F-16 research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including Appendices A-C in v1 and A-D in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original F-16 benchmark and sports-understanding results, inference measurements, and aligner ablations in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original F-16 experiments, inference measurements, and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.3 retain the same high-frame-rate aligner, initialization, spatial pooling, and frame-repetition decoding procedure. No proposed algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same general-video benchmarks and gymnastics, diving, basketball, and soccer tasks. Appendix D illustrates an existing Diving48 example without expanding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 1, the sports comparisons, and appendix experiments. MiniCPM-V2.6-8B already appears in v1; its newly added citation does not introduce a baseline.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes the reported frame counts for LLaVA-Video-7B from 32 to 64 and NVILA-7B from 256 to 1024. These revise stated comparison settings; the PDFs do not establish that the experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix D compares frames from one randomly sampled Diving48 clip at 1, 4, and 16 FPS, providing a limited qualitative illustration of temporal detail captured by different sampling rates. Existing ablations and captioning cases remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The reporting of statistical uncertainty is unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes LLaVA-OV-7B's MLVU m-Avg score from 51.4 to 64.7. F-16 remains at 70.3 on that metric, and the remaining quantitative performance results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, initialization derivation, and decoding equations are retained, including Equations (1)-(11). No theoretical argument or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The claims concerning high-frame-rate video understanding, leading performance among 7B models, sports understanding, and training-free variable-frame-rate decoding retain the same meaning and scope.

C2.justification: Explanations of long-video weaknesses, pooling-related information loss, and alternative aligners' limitations are retained. Appendix D illustrates the existing sampling motivation without introducing a new mechanism explanation or limitation.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the release-upon-acceptance statement with a planned release at the bytedance/F-16 GitHub repository for code, checkpoints, and data. This supplies a specific access location but does not establish that resources have been released.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yao et al. (2024), MiniCPM-V, to the introduction and bibliography. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short Appendix D and its cross-reference, revises the abstract's release sentence, and updates correspondence and conference front matter. The main narrative and section organization are substantially retained.

P2.justification: Figures 4-6 add diving-frame montages at three sampling rates. Table 10 moves upward to share a page with new figures, with limited pagination and text reflow elsewhere; existing figure and table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides a concrete visual illustration of the sampling motivation, a specific planned-release location, and additional MiniCPM-V attribution. These modestly improve explanation and traceability. The method and quantitative validation of F-16 remain unchanged, and resource release is still prospective.
